framingRule.whatIsTrue: evidence.v10 -- the OWNING surface for SemanticEvidenceV1 -- genuinely does not state it. The one field in the whole grammar that carries an 'encoding' key is RawProofInventoryV1.items, the nested list. Nothing in evidence.v10 maps a 'type' onto scalarEncoding.text. And evaluation-proof.v8#normativePreimageGrammar.records declares 'encoding': 'componentFrame(text)' on approximately forty fields, including precisely the typed identity and reference values at issue -- ActivationManifestV1.projectId, .planId, .planIntentCommitment, .executionPlanCommitment, .resolvedActivationGraphRef; EvaluationAuthoritySealV1.activationManifestRef; VerdictInputV2.outcomeSetCommitment and .waiverSetCommitment; WaiverV1.waiverRef; BaselineV1.baselineRef. If no artifact states the rule, someone must DECIDE it and the decision is a design act reserved by section 7.1. The subject sent the corpus down the first path. That error has ALREADY PROPAGATED: IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md at d35c283b now asserts in its own section 7.1 narrative that the rule is 'nowhere stated in prose' and that 'no artifact says which.' DIV1.question: The measured consequence: under deduplicate, does the multiset [a,a,b] and the set [a,b] yield one identical digest while subjectCount is a separate unbound field? And was adopting evidence.v10's REJECT correct, or should the subject have transcribed evaluation-proof.v8 exactly and raised the divergence as a finding?
DIV1.measurementVERIFIED: YES, EXACTLY AS CLAIMED. Independently computed with the third encoder: under the deduplicate rule the subject multiset ['a','a','b'] and the set ['a','b'] both yield sha256:6c73ad6ac599e006513f4b8bf2e12e9149a7b64b370fe010395fb6b19c0b3519. BYTE-EQUAL. The subject's SS-5 publishes both under different key names and they are the same string, which is precisely 'two different logical values produce one preimage'. Under the adopted REJECT rule the multiset raises and has no image. Both source verbatims also verified: evaluation-proof.v8#normativePreimageGrammar.commitment.itemSetRule reads 'deduplicate exact record bytes, then sort unsigned bytewise ascending'; evidence.v10#canonicalWireGrammar.recordRules.sets reads 'sort complete item record bytes unsigned; reject duplicates instead of silently deduplicating'. Both quoted exactly by the subject.
DIV1.andOBS4VERIFIED: subjectCount is indeed an independent unbound field: evaluation-proof.v8#positiveVectors[EP8-POS-NOMATCH-PASS].bundle.evaluations[0].proof carries subjectCount 3 alongside subjectSetCommitment, and nothing in TCMS-V5 binds them.
DIV1.ruling: ADOPTING REJECT WAS CORRECT. The objection the subject expects against itself -- 'R-0 is faithful to neither source' -- is OVERSTATED AGAINST ITSELF, and the subject would have seen that had it read one key further into its own source.
DIV1.whyTheSelfObjectionFails: evaluation-proof.v8 is NOT univocally a deduplicate grammar. Its OWN normativePreimageGrammar.recordRules.duplicates reads, verbatim: 'duplicate scalar fields and duplicate logical list members are forbidden'. FORBIDDEN, not deduplicated. So evaluation-proof.v8 contains BOTH dispositions: commitment.itemSetRule says deduplicate at the Merkle-set layer, recordRules.duplicates says forbid at the nested-list layer. The adopted REJECT is therefore faithful to evidence.v10 AND to evaluation-proof.v8's recordRules, and dissents only from evaluation-proof.v8's itemSetRule. 'Faithful to neither source' is wrong; the accurate statement is 'faithful to both surfaces' record rules and to one of two mutually inconsistent clauses inside evaluation-proof.v8'.
DIV1.andThereforeDIV1IsSharperThanStated: DIV-1 is not only a divergence BETWEEN two artifacts. It is ALSO an internal inconsistency WITHIN evaluation-proof.v8. That is a finding against evaluation-proof.v8 which this review records and which the subject did not make. It strengthens the case for REJECT: the deduplicate clause is the outlier, not the consensus.
DIV1.shouldItHaveTranscribedEP8EXACTLYINSTEAD: NO. Transcribing 'deduplicate' would have published a construction the subject had MEASURED to be non-injective on its declared domain -- SS-5 proves the multiset and the set collide. A byte recipe whose author has measured a collision and publishes it anyway, silently, is the defect this corpus exists to prevent. Publishing BOTH outcomes and flagging reviewerMustDecide is the correct disposition and this reviewer endorses it.
DIV1.unresolvedRemains: The divergence is NOT resolved by this review. Only the owning surfaces can reconcile it. Recorded as a condition on closure, not as a blocker against the subject.

DIV2.question: Is the difference between evidence.v1's fact-tuple digest leaves and evaluation-proof.v8's raw path text leaves a real difference in privacy posture, and is raw path text in a durable Merkle leaf consistent with the blueprint's requirement that secrets be represented by handles only?
DIV2.sourcesVERIFIEDVERBATIM: YES, both quoted correctly by the subject. evidence.v1#noMatchConstruction.construction.subjectSetCommitment.what reads 'A Merkle root over the SORTED list of subject identities, where a subject identity is the content digest of that subject's normalised fact tuple'; .notSourceBytes reads 'The leaves are digests of FACTS, not of source. A fact tuple is already a lossy structural projection'; .whySorted reads 'A sorted-leaf Merkle tree yields NON-membership proofs from adjacent-leaf paths.' And evaluation-proof.v8#preimageGoldens.records[EP5-REC-SUBJECT].encodedHex is 1305000000087372632f612e7473, containing the literal ASCII 'src/a.ts'.
DIV2.ruling: IT IS A REAL AND MATERIAL DIFFERENCE IN PRIVACY POSTURE, CORRECTLY IDENTIFIED AND CORRECTLY ESCALATED. It is NOT a defect of this artifact and it is NOT a blocker against it. It IS a blocking condition on relying on R-4, and this review records it as such. The subject earned no pass for disclosing it -- it earned a pass because resolving it was not its to resolve.
DIV2.onTheSECRETSASHANDLESTEST: The blueprint obligation 'requested read-set allowlist, exact projects/<ProjectId> ledger/CAS isolation, secrets represented by handles only' is at IMPLEMENTER-BLUEPRINT.md section 8.1, first owner 'resolver + snapshot + store', early gate G14. NOTE FOR THE RECORD: it is NOT at blueprint section 1.1 in the current bytes -- section 1.1 at a8689925 is the normative byte-set table. RULING ON THE TEST ITSELF: raw path text does NOT violate secrets-as-handles on a plain reading. A source path is not a credential, and the obligation is about secret MATERIAL being held by handle. Reaching for that clause OVERSTATES the case and this reviewer declines to file it as a violation.
DIV2.whereTheREALPROBLEMIS: The real problem is retention shape, not secret handling, and it is WORSE than the subject states. The subject frames DIV-2 as 'raw subject text in a leaf'. A leaf PREIMAGE need not be retained -- only the root must be. But evaluation-proof.v8's bundle retains the subject list IN THE CLEAR at bundle.partitionContents[0].members = ['src/a.ts','src/b.ts','src/c.ts'], durably, because a verifier must recompute the commitment. So for a no-match claim quantified over a repository, the durable evidence retains THE FILE INVENTORY OF THAT REPOSITORY as plaintext. That is source-derived material at a size proportional to the subject set -- and evidence.v1's construction exists precisely to argue that no-match evidence stays ~100 bytes per evaluation 'INDEPENDENT of subject count' and three to five orders of magnitude below a source archive. Under source A that cost and privacy argument does not hold. The subject located the divergence in the leaf; it actually lives in the bundle.
DIV2.whyTheSUBJECTWASRIGHTNOTTORESOLVEIT: Adopting source B would have required INVENTING a fact-tuple normalisation and digest that no live artifact defines, to produce digests no vector pins. That is exactly the act section 7.1 forbids. Adopting source A and disclosing at severity 'CHANGES THE PRIVACY POSTURE OF THE NO-MATCH CONSTRUCTION' is the only honest move available to an authoring agent.
DIV2.additionalGapNEITHERSOURCECLOSES: evidence.v1's ONLY stated justification for sorting is non-membership proofs from adjacent-leaf paths. R-4 transcribes the sort and specifies NO AUDIT-PATH FORMAT. Under the promote-unchanged odd-node rule an audit path is non-uniform and its verification requires the leaf count N, which the commitment does not bind. The subject correctly notes cardinality is not needed for INJECTIVITY -- this reviewer verified that independently -- but does not note it IS needed for the PROOF the sort exists to enable. Whoever resolves DIV-2 must resolve this too, or the sorting rule is carrying a rationale the construction cannot deliver.

noRetainedChecker.question: 'A byte recipe with no retained checker is a description that happens to contain digests.' Is that disqualifying for a v1 candidate, or a fair residual?
noRetainedChecker.ruling: A FAIR RESIDUAL FOR A CANDIDATE. DISQUALIFYING FOR APPLICATION OR FOR CLOSING A SECTION 7.1 ROW. It is NOT counted among this review's blockers.
noRetainedChecker.whyNotDisqualifyingNOW: Three reasons, in order of weight. FIRST AND DECISIVE: the objection's premise is that the digests may be unreproducible prose. This reviewer TESTED that premise and it FAILED -- a third encoder, written from the subject's prose alone, sharing no code with the author, reproduced all 26 vectors across 52 assertions on the first run with zero failures. The property a retained checker would automate was DEMONSTRATED HERE, by hand, by someone else. That is not equivalent to an instrument, but it is not nothing, and it is exactly the check reviewerChecklist item 2 asked for. SECOND: the artifact binds nothing, self-declares DO-NOT-SEAL and CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED, and asserts no closure. B-VER9R-01's failure mode is a SEALED surface whose evidence silently rots; a candidate awaiting review is not yet in that position. THIRD: requiring a retained checker as a precondition of FIRST REVIEW would invert this corpus's own order of operations -- every checker here was written against bytes that had already been reviewed at least once.
noRetainedChecker.whyDISQUALIFYINGLATER: The staleness risk is REAL and is already materialising, which is the part the subject understates. Seven of the 26 vectors -- the only seven not authored in the subject's own pass, and therefore the only seven that are not self-referential -- are pinned against evaluation-proof.v8 and evidence.v10, BOTH of which are CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED and both of which are under active revision (evaluation-proof has reached v13; evidence has reached v10 with a v11/v12/v13 lineage on disk). When either moves, those seven vectors become assertions about bytes nobody applied, and NOTHING IN THIS CORPUS WILL NOTICE. nonBlockingObservations.title: The injectivity proof is one step short of its conclusion, though the conclusion holds
nonBlockingObservations.detail: sharedPrimitives.injectivityByInverse argues: a total decoder exists, decode(encode(x)) == x, therefore encode has a left inverse, therefore encode is injective. But the exhibited decoder recovers FIELD BYTE STRINGS -- it 'reads uint8(tag), uint32be(len) and exactly len bytes'. It never inverts the value-to-bytes step. So the round trip establishes that the FRAMING is injective; it does not by itself establish that the map from LOGICAL VALUES to bytes is injective. That second half rests on two other rules the artifact does state but does not fold into the argument: reject-rather-than-normalize for text, and canonicalUnsignedDecimal for integers.
nonBlockingObservations.verifiedIndependently: The CONCLUSION is correct and this reviewer confirmed it empirically. Demonstrated: if an implementation NORMALIZED instead of rejecting, the NFD and NFC spellings of 'cafe'+combining-acute both encode to 130500000005636166c3a9 -- one preimage, two logical values, NON-INJECTIVE. Under the artifact's REJECT rule the NFD form raises and has no image, so injectivity is preserved. The artifact's rule is right; its stated proof just does not reach it.
nonBlockingObservations.why: Recorded because the artifact holds itself to jx_canon's standard and this is the one place the argument is looser than the claim.

nonBlockingObservations.title: OBS-5's tag enumeration is incomplete; its conclusion survives

Second and more substantive, evaluation-proof.v8's goldens carry items in record-tag position at 0x60 and 0x70 -- preimageGoldens.commitments[EP5-COMMIT-CAPABILITY-CLOSURE-GENERIC].itemEncodedHex is '6000000000' and [EP5-COMMIT-SEMANTIC-CAPABILITY-CLOSURE-V3-GENERIC] is '7000000000', neither of which appears in normativePreimageGrammar.records.

The subject is also right that the disjointness is an ACCIDENT of independent authorship rather than a stated invariant, and right to say so.

nonBlockingObservations.title: Two R-1 vector inputs are not declared, so the vectors are not reproducible strictly 'from the declared inputs'

nonBlockingObservations.title: DIV-1 is also an internal inconsistency inside evaluation-proof.v8, which the subject did not notice
nonBlockingObservations.detail: evaluation-proof.v8#normativePreimageGrammar.recordRules.duplicates reads verbatim 'duplicate scalar fields and duplicate logical list members are forbidden', while the same grammar's commitment.itemSetRule reads 'deduplicate exact record bytes, then sort unsigned bytewise ascending'. nonBlockingObservations.title: Everything I could throw at injectivity and domain separation held
nonBlockingObservations.detail: Reported because a reviewer's failed attacks are evidence. ATTEMPTED AND DEFEATED: (a) cross-cardinality root collision -- all 1024 subsets of a 10-element subject universe produce 1024 DISTINCT roots, zero collisions, and leaf counts N=0..17 produce 17 distinct roots; (b) promote-unchanged ambiguity -- an iterative and an independently written recursive fold agree for every N from 1 to 32, and the classic promote-versus-pair confusion is blocked because a promoted node is a leaf hash (preimage byte 0x00) or internal hash (0x01) and the two can never be exchanged; (c) empty-set confusion -- the empty root's preimage begins 0x02 and cannot be a leaf, an internal node or an outer frame; (d) single-element -- the root IS a leaf hash, and node-type separation is what makes that safe rather than decorative, exactly as the subject argues; (e) cross-context reuse -- one identical Merkle root framed under all nine members of the closed domain vocabulary yields nine distinct commitments, and the TCMS outer frame (byte 0 = 0x30) can never be confused with the R-1 DomainEnvelopeV1 frame (byte 0 = 0x8e); (f) domain boundary slide -- length framing defeats it, reproduced at ED-6 including both full preimage hexes; (g) field boundary slide -- reproduced at UC-6-A/B; (h) empty and control-character values -- rejected as specified; (i) astral-plane and combining-sequence subjects -- encode and fold correctly under the stated rules.
nonBlockingObservations.theOneIcouldNOTDefeat: None of the encoding attacks succeeded. The strongest attack I could not defeat is not an encoding attack at all -- see whatIDidNotCheck.theAttackIcouldNotClose.

nonBlockingObservations.title: DIV-2's disclosure risk is understated and the sorting rationale is unrealised
nonBlockingObservations.detail: TWO refinements to DIV-2, both in the direction of MORE serious. FIRST: the subject frames the exposure as 'raw subject text in a leaf', but a leaf preimage need not be retained -- only the root must be. The actual retention is at evaluation-proof.v8#positiveVectors[EP8-POS-NOMATCH-PASS].bundle.partitionContents[0].members, which holds ['src/a.ts','src/b.ts','src/c.ts'] in plaintext durably, because a verifier must recompute the commitment. Scaled to a repository-wide no-match, the durable evidence retains the repository's file inventory -- defeating evidence.v1's stated cost argument that no-match evidence is '~100 bytes, INDEPENDENT of subject count'. SECOND: evidence.v1's sole justification for sorting is non-membership proofs from adjacent-leaf paths, and R-4 specifies NO audit-path format. Under promote-unchanged an audit path is non-uniform and its verification needs the leaf count N, which the commitment does not bind. The subject correctly notes cardinality is unnecessary for INJECTIVITY -- verified -- but not that it is necessary for the PROOF the sort exists to enable.
nonBlockingObservations.why: Whoever adjudicates DIV-2 needs both. Neither is a defect the subject could have repaired.

nonBlockingObservations.title: Law 18 self-application verified, and the admission that no vector can enforce it is COMPLETE
nonBlockingObservations.detail: numericRepresentationRule claims zero JSON numbers and zero JSON booleans at any leaf. VERIFIED BY FULL RECURSIVE WALK of the exact subject bytes: 796 leaves, 0 numbers, 0 booleans, and additionally 0 nulls, which the subject does not claim but which closes the adjacent respelling position. The claim is exactly true and 'derive, do not enumerate' really is applied to the artifact's own bytes.
nonBlockingObservations.isTheADMISSIONCOMPLETE: YES, and this reviewer tried to find the hole. typeAdmissionIsNotTheDigestsJob states that an implementation coercing 1.0 to 1 before encoding produces the correct byte 0x31 and therefore the correct digest, so the vector passes while law 18 is violated. That is correct and it generalises further than the subject spells out: the SAME argument defeats a vector for EVERY scalar position in every recipe -- a boolean true coerced to the enum text, a numeric string '1' coerced to 1, an integer-valued float in the inventory schemaVersion. The subject's statement covers the general case by naming the mechanism (a digest cannot police its input's JSON type) rather than the instance, which is the correct form. NO ADDITIONAL EXPOSURE IS CONCEALED BY THE NARROWER PHRASING.
nonBlockingObservations.residual: The precondition -- that these recipes are defined only over records that have already passed exact-type admission -- is DECLARED and UNTESTED, and by construction untestable from inside a byte recipe. That is honest and correctly placed.

nonBlockingObservations.title: The subject understates its own strongest evidence in three places
nonBlockingObservations.detail: Recorded in fairness, since an adversarial review that reports only overstatement is not measuring. (a) The framing rule is corroborated by evaluation-proof.v8's prose and its independent goldens, and is FORCED by evidence.v10's own pinned scalar lengths -- the subject calls it merely 'strong but not a citation'. (b) The outcomeSetDigest identification is supported by two CURRENT documents, not only by superseded evidence.v2 as the subject assumes. (c) The adopted REJECT duplicate rule is faithful to evaluation-proof.v8's recordRules.duplicates, not 'faithful to NEITHER source' as the subject's own third-strongest objection concedes. In all three the subject argued AGAINST its own position more strongly than the corpus warrants. That is the correct direction for an author to err, and it is still an inaccuracy.

items: I did NOT verify that evidence.v10 or evaluation-proof.v8 are CORRECT as contracts. Both are CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED and neither was reviewed here. I verified only that the subject transcribes them faithfully, with the two exceptions recorded as blockers. DUD-1 and DUD-2 are therefore CONFIRMED AS DECLARED and remain live: every recipe here still transcribes from an unapplied source, and if either source is replaced, all four recipes lose their basis. That is a property of the corpus, not a defect of the subject, and it is correctly declared.

I did NOT verify DUD-5's canonical-JSON claim. I did not reproduce evaluationProofBundleCasRef sha256:cc27c2be... from the EP8 bundle, and I did not check whether c2-plan-stage-schema.v4's opensip-canonical-json-v1 is the rule evidence.v10 means. R-1 treats that value as an opaque input and so did I. The subject's own caveat -- that an all-ASCII bundle cannot distinguish escaping policies for non-ASCII, nor key-sort by Unicode scalar value from key-sort by UTF-8 bytes -- is correct and I did not narrow it.

I did NOT adjudicate DUD-6. Whether C-2's Coverage-key subjectScopeCommitment is the same thing as the EVALUATION-PROOF subject-set commitment is a cross-surface judgement between C-2, RETENTION and EVIDENCE. The subject explicitly does not claim it and I did not decide it. The literal section 7.1 subjectScopeCommitment row is therefore UNADDRESSED by the subject and UNADDRESSED by this review.

I did NOT verify DUD-7 or DUD-8 beyond confirming the subject's characterisation. I did not audit the RT22 recordKind vocabulary or search for a current owner of the outcome vocabulary. Both are correctly declared as unresolved.

I did NOT test non-ASCII against the SOURCE GRAMMARS' intent. My encoder accepts astral-plane and combining-sequence subjects under the subject's stated rules, but no vector in the corpus pins a non-ASCII digest, so I confirmed only that the rules are WELL-DEFINED over such input -- not that any owning surface AGREES with the result. The subject's own recommendation, that a reviewer ask for vectors over combining sequences and astral-plane subjects, is correct and I second it. THE NFC REJECT-VERSUS-NORMALIZE CHOICE IS PARTICULARLY EXPOSED: evidence.v10#recordRules.decoding does say 'reject non-NFC', but evaluation-proof.v8 says only 'NFC-normalized UTF-8' and does not disambiguate, so R-0's inherited reject rule rests on the EVIDENCE surface's wording applied to an EVALUATION-PROOF construction. No vector distinguishes them because every vector is ASCII.

I did NOT exercise the fold above 32 leaves, and no published vector exceeds four set elements plus the 23-element inventory sort. I extended the subject's coverage from four to 32 and found nothing; the recursion is uniform and I have no reason to suspect a defect above that, but I did not look.

I did NOT re-derive the subject's claim of 96 digest comparisons by its own two encoders. That count describes an execution I did not witness and cannot reproduce, because neither encoder is retained anywhere in this repository. I replaced it with 52 comparisons of my own rather than confirming it. THE 96 REMAINS AN UNVERIFIED SELF-REPORT -- which is precisely the shape section 7.2.2 warns about, and precisely what a retained checker would fix.

I did NOT re-read the whole of IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md at d35c283b. I re-verified section 7.1 and the three load-bearing facts directly, and read the new narrative at lines 1288-1334. If any moved, the affected reasoning is unverified -- the same disclosure the subject makes, now inherited by this review one drift later.

I did NOT evaluate the product questions. CD-RT-5, the V10 default, purge semantics and every [UNSET] disposition are untouched and unexamined. The subject correctly asserts it is not gated on any of them and I did not test that assertion beyond confirming it changes none of them.

THE ATTACK I COULD NOT CLOSE -- not an encoding attack, every one of those failed. The attack I cannot close is the one R-1's own whyTwoDifferentLogicalValuesCannotShareAPreimage[5] declares as a residual: injectivity is proven on the RECORD, and the record's thirteen field VALUES are typed identities minted on other surfaces. If two semantically distinct evaluations could ever produce identical values in all thirteen fields, they share an EvidenceDigest. Whether the thirteen fields SUFFICE to distinguish semantically distinct evidence is a contract question about evidence.v10's field set. It cannot be settled by any byte recipe, it cannot be settled by any vector, and it is not settled here. The subject declares it accurately and does not overclaim past it; I could not close it and neither could it.
